prompt:
# Subject Merge Fine Clustering

## Quick Start

Inside one topic area, create tight candidate clusters that are worth a later same-concept decision. Use only the provided candidate cards.

## Identity Filter

Cluster candidates only when they might be the same teachable idea at the same level, testable with the same question.

Do not cluster just because candidates share a keyword. Keep candidates separate when one adds implementation, math, limitation, application, deeper mechanism, tool-specific behavior, or a broader/narrower student action.

Doubt means singleton. Under-clustering is safer than sending unrelated candidates to merge evaluation.

## Output

Return one JSON object only:

```json
{
  "clusters": [
    {
      "id": "cluster_001",
      "label": "Short candidate cluster",
      "rationale": "Why these candidates may share concept identity.",
      "candidate_ids": ["candidate-id"]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Self-Check

- Every input candidate ID appears exactly once.
- Each non-singleton cluster has a plausible same-concept reason.
- Implementation, limitation, application, math, and deeper-revisit candidates were not grouped with definitions just because labels overlap.
- Mixed-language same-level candidates were clustered when their teachable idea matches.
- No web search or external knowledge was used.

area.label: Principles of Effective Decision-Making
area.rationale: Candidates describe core qualities of great decisions, including seeking diverse viewpoints, acting close to the action, addressing root causes, assigning accountability, balancing short- and long-term value, communicating effectively, making timely decisions, and balancing gut with team considerations. Together they form a coherent set of best practices for individual decision-making.

candidates.label: Consider Many Different Viewpoints in Decision-Making
candidates.description: Great decisions are shaped by consideration of many different viewpoints, without seeking consensus but not acting unilaterally; it requires discernment on whose opinion to seek and when to force a solution.
coverage_criteria: Explain why considering many different viewpoints shapes great decisions.
Describe how to balance seeking input versus making a unilateral decision.
candidates.lesson_title: Decision-making process and fundamentals of decision-making approaches.

candidates.label: Make Decisions Close to the Action
candidates.description: Great decisions are made as close as possible to the action, involving those who do the work rather than only those in power, which requires trust and putting ego aside.
coverage_criteria: Describe why involving front-line workers improves decision quality.
Identify situations where it is better to seek advice from those at the operational level.
candidates.lesson_title: Decision-making process and fundamentals of decision-making approaches.

candidates.label: Address Root Cause in Decision-Making
candidates.description: Great decisions address the root cause of problems, not just symptoms, by engaging people who understand where issues originated and developing plans to fix the underlying cause.
coverage_criteria: Differentiate between symptoms and root causes in a decision context.
Explain why focusing on root causes leads to more effective decisions.
candidates.lesson_title: Decision-making process and fundamentals of decision-making approaches.

candidates.label: Assign Clear Accountability in Decisions
candidates.description: Great decisions are made by a clearly accountable person who stands behind their decisions, even if they later turn out to be mistakes.
coverage_criteria: Explain the importance of clear accountability in decision-making.
Describe how accountability fosters ownership and integrity in the decision process.
candidates.lesson_title: Decision-making process and fundamentals of decision-making approaches.

candidates.label: Balance Short-Term and Long-Term Value in Decisions
candidates.description: Great decisions consider the holistic impacts of a problem and balance long-term and short-term value, sometimes requiring sacrifice of immediate efficiency for long-term competence.
coverage_criteria: Discuss how to evaluate trade-offs between short-term gains and long-term value in decision-making.
Provide examples where short-term sacrifices lead to long-term benefits.
candidates.lesson_title: Decision-making process and fundamentals of decision-making approaches.

candidates.label: Communicate Decisions Effectively to Stakeholders
candidates.description: Great decisions are communicated well to stakeholders, involving honesty and integrity even when facing difficult audiences or consequences.
coverage_criteria: Outline key principles for effectively communicating decisions to stakeholders.
Explain the importance of transparency and integrity in decision communication.
candidates.lesson_title: Decision-making process and fundamentals of decision-making approaches.

candidates.label: Make Timely Decisions
candidates.description: Great decisions are timely; they avoid procrastination, fear of mistakes, or blame-shifting by charting the best course forward with available information and acting promptly.
coverage_criteria: Explain the importance of timeliness in decision-making.
Identify common barriers to timely decisions such as perfectionism or fear of disapproval.
candidates.lesson_title: Decision-making process and fundamentals of decision-making approaches.

candidates.label: Balance Gut Instinct with Team Considerations
candidates.description: While trusting one's gut can be valuable, great decisions also require considering whether that instinct is the best course for everyone involved.
coverage_criteria: Discuss the role of intuition in decision-making.
Describe when it is appropriate to rely on gut instinct versus when broader team or organizational considerations should prevail.
candidates.lesson_title: Decision-making process and fundamentals of decision-making approaches.

candidate_assignment_rule: Cluster only. Every input candidate ID must appear exactly once across clusters. Prefer tight clusters; topic overlap alone is not a cluster.

web_access_policy.instruction: Do not use web search or open URLs. Use only the provided candidate cards.
